guard_streams.source: Broadband complaints fall to record low
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint rates are service-quality indicators. They do not establish physical broadband availability, live orderability or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the update on 23 July 2026.
The latest figures cover January to March 2026.
Broadband complaints reached an all-time low of six per 100,000 customers.
The article compares this with a 2011 peak of 40 complaints per 100,000 customers.
Collective complaints across landline, broadband, mobile and pay-TV decreased from Q4 2025.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about broadband provider.
TalkTalk complaints mainly concerned faults, service and provisioning, complaint handling, and billing or charges.
Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed-broadband complaints.
Ofcom states it cannot act on individual complaints.
Ofcom says complaint data can help customers compare providers when considered with price, availability and quality.

guard_streams.source: Comparing customer service: choosing the best home broadband, mobile and landline provider
guard_streams.write_limit: Customer-service comparisons, satisfaction measures and provider fault statistics are not selected-parcel coverage or measured-speed evidence.

facts.detail: The comparison page was published on 18 May 2023.
The page was last updated on 25 May 2026.
The current publication is Ofcom's eighth customer-service comparison report.
It covers residential telecom customer service levels and experiences in 2024.
It compares 2024 results with 2022 and/or 2023.
Ofcom moved from annual to biennial reporting after the 2023 report.
Overall satisfaction among mobile, broadband and landline customers remained high.
Overall satisfaction with complaint handling increased significantly in 2024 compared with 2022.
The report found mixed results for broadband and landline faults.
EE resubmitted certain 2024 fault data in April 2026, leaving some report figures subject to restatement.

guard_streams.source: Quicker complaints resolution for telecoms customers, under new Ofcom rules
guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint-resolution rules concern consumer redress, not physical broadband coverage, orderability or selected-parcel performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the rules update on 8 July 2025.
The strengthened rules apply to residential and small-business telecom customers.
ADR schemes independently and impartially assess unresolved complaints.
Ofcom launched its ADR-system review in November 2023.
The previous rules required an ADR letter after eight unresolved weeks.
Between January 2022 and 2024, 79% of complaints at the biggest telecom companies were resolved in under a week.
Ninety-four percent were resolved within six weeks.
Around 700,000 consumers had complaints still open at six weeks.
Ofcom reduced the ADR access threshold from eight weeks to six.
The six-week rule took effect on 8 April 2026.
